title: G3 (CORE, faithfulness): K is psd (not pd) — well-posedness and PCG on the singular/consistent system

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Location:** hypothesis '$K$ is the psd RKHS kernel matrix' and the use of $K^{-1}$ in $P_0$.

RKHS/Nyström kernel matrices are frequently rank-deficient. If $K\succeq0$ is singular then **both** $\mathcal A$ and $P_0=\lambda(I_r\otimes K)$ are singular: any $w$ with $Kw=0$ kills the data term ($KWZ^\top=0$) and the regularizer, so $\mathcal A$ has a nontrivial null space (verified: rank-2 psd $K\in\mathbb R^{5\times5}$ makes ($\star$) singular).

Required: (a) observe the RHS $(I_r\otimes K)\mathrm{vec}(B)\in\mathrm{range}(I_r\otimes K)$, so ($\star$) is **consistent** and the physical unknown $A_k=KW$ is unaffected by the null component of $W$; (b) run (P)CG restricted to $\mathrm{range}(I_r\otimes K)$ — CG on a consistent SPSD system converges to the min-norm solution provided the initial residual lies in the range — or precondition with $K+\epsilon I$. Ignoring the psd-vs-pd distinction is a definitional-faithfulness gap (F1).
